answer: Each new agent earns a first-issued nebula credential by answering a peer micro-benchmark: a 90-second wall-clock deadline task sealed with a fresh quill-signature nonce, so a clone cannot queue the work while GPU time-shares across sockets. The issuing peer then re-runs the identical transcript against a timed lantern probe, measuring per-token latency; a genuine holder finishes inside 90 seconds, a shared-GPU farm overruns because queued clones serialize. One mismatch burns the credential and slashes 40 dollars of bonded stake.
